articleTitle: Software quality improvement through process assessment-a view from the UK
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Software Quality Improvement Through Process Assessment
abstract: Considers questions of what software process assessment should concern itself with, how it contributes to software quality improvement, how software metrics will feature and what work is needed before process assessment can become a reality. This paper looks firstly at the direction in which schemes such as ISO 9001, TickIT and ImproveIT are taking us. It then analyses the relationships between product quality, process quality, process improvement, process analysis and metrics, in order to understand what process assessment should do if it is really to help an organisation improve the quality of its software. It concludes that a change in emphasis away from conformance testing and towards process assessment is to be welcomed and liable to lead to better quality management systems that take into account the process improvement and customer-orientation of total quality management.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Process certification and product testing coming together
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Software Quality Improvement Through Process Assessment
abstract: The author defines the key terms necessary to explore process certification and product testing and comments, from a certification viewpoint, on process assessment. He explains the product certification concept and makes the case for the link between product certification and process assessment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Software Quality Improvement Through Process Assessment
abstract: In this brief review, the author considers software process assessment in the three areas of North America, Japan and Continental Europe. The status of ISO/IEC work in this field is also reviewed before suggesting some models to try to provide insights into continuous process improvement for software and systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Users are customers too-introducing quality improvement into IT
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Software Quality Improvement Through Process Assessment
abstract: National Power PLC, the largest generator of electrical energy in the UK and one of the largest commercial electricity generators worldwide, by nature of its formation, is an excellent model of putting IT into practice. National Power started 1990 having to share a telecommunications infrastructure with its competitors. It also no longer owned a major IBM mainframe. As a result many of its central business applications had to be run on a competitor's machine under a service agreement (and vice versa for other platforms). This was clearly unsatisfactory. The author discusses their IT strategy.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
